messages:
Alex: ran an nsight capture for the long-tail spike seen on prod inference. attaching timeline snippet. weird: big host->device memcpy lines overlap/precede attention kernels but GPUs show low SM utilization.

Maria: can you paste the nsys command you used? also which workload (seq len / batch)?

Alex: seq=512, microbatch=1, batcher=continuous, model=huggingface/our-llm-v2. command:
```
nsys profile --output=trace_1718004321 --trace=cuda,cudnn,osrt,host --sample=cpu,none --capture-range=stop -- python -m run_infer --config prod.json
```

Dan: looked at the timeline -> I see a long cudaMemcpyAsync on stream 1 (~120ms) starting right after a small kernel finishes. Then kernels scheduled on stream 3 stall for ~110ms. stream priorities look correct but copy engine is serializing with kernel launches.

Sam: that smells like pinned buffer shortage or host side CPU sleep delaying the enqueue of copies. do you see many `cudaHostAlloc`/pinned allocations in the trace?

Alex: no pinned allocs during steady state, we use a pinned pool but it shows repeated small host copies instead of one batched H2D. snippet from trace (simplified):
```
[0.000s] kernel attention_fwd stream 3 (1.2ms)
[0.002s] memcpy H2D cudaMemcpyAsync stream 1 (120.3ms) size=18MB
[0.122s] kernel matmul_gemm stream 3 (0.7ms) queued but not running
[0.123s] cpu scheduling gap main_thread (80ms)
[0.203s] kernel attention_fwd stream 3 (1.1ms) resumes
```

Maria: CPU scheduling gap @main_thread ~80ms is suspicious. if the user thread is preempted between preparing the next batch and issuing the H2D, the copy start gets delayed until CPU wakes, making the copy appear long and overlapping other streams.

Dan: another possibility: host-to-device copy uses default stream or stream 1 with higher priority but copy engine handshake with kernels on different engines causes serialization. On some drivers a blocking hostcopy (synchronous or non-pinned) can force serialization across engines.

Alex: I grep'd the trace for `cudaMemcpy` vs `cudaMemcpyAsync` — it's Async from code, but we still see the long runtime. Notably the host stack shows repeated `epoll_wait` and then immediate syscalls to submit. so the thread was sleeping.

Sam: actionables I suggest: 1) enforce pinned buffer allocation warmup (pre-alloc pool) 2) switch H2D to use a dedicated copy stream with highest priority and test `cudaMemcpyAsync` with pinned memory 3) run with `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=0` and driver trace to confirm copy engine backlog.

Maria: also try changing batcher config to aggregate prefetches: REDWOOD_BATCHER_PREFETCH_WINDOW=2 so multiple token batches issue a single larger H2D instead of many small copies. small copies amplify CPU scheduling jitter.

Alex: tried prefetch_window=2 locally — tail drops ~30% but not eliminated. Next I ran `perf record -g -p <pid>` on host, saw heavy context switches in the user thread right before memcpy submission.

Dan: we should also look at kernel selection: I see attention_fwd kernel variants in trace: `att_fwd_fp16_fast` vs `att_fwd_fp16_ref`. The runtime picks `fast` but it has larger workspace leading to more H2D for KV cache prefetch. fallback `ref` uses less host copy but slightly slower compute. Might be a tradeoff.

Sam: good catch. runtime kernel selector could consider end-to-end latency (hostcopy + compute) instead of kernel-only perf. We can add a simple heuristic: if predicted hostcopy > X ms, prefer lower-memory kernel.

Alex: created a short repro run and uploaded qdrep to perf-bot. perf-bot: new capture available at /artifacts/nsys/1718004321.qdrep :thumbsup:

perf-bot: uploaded /artifacts/nsys/1718004321.qdrep (size 48MB) :file_folder:

Maria: next steps: Alex to script a bisect that toggles kernel variant + prefetch_window + pinned pool size. Dan to add a metric to batcher telemetry that reports per-request H2D time. Sam to draft heuristic pseudo for kernel selector.

Alex: will do. for immediate fix we rolled a config bump to pre-allocate pinned pool + increase prefetch_window to 2 in staging. will monitor. thanks all :rocket:
